cultural.vision_reason: Documentary photo of Hill Anga men and boys at a harvest celebration, drumming and playing horns, wearing loin-cloths, caps, personal ornaments, and patterned cloth — a clear ethnographic scene of the claimed group's dress and customs.

physical.title: photographic print
physical.summary:
Nigeria, view of large group of male Hill Anga adults and children at "harvest celebrations in the market square". Male at centre playing drum, using what appears to animal's tail. Several males playing horns. Most males wearing caps, personal-ornaments, loin-cloths, patterned cloth across shoulder. Male at left wearing animal-hide around waist. Drummer wearing head-dress. Large, thatched-roof building in background.
Medium: Gelatin silver print.
Format: One of four prints mounted on album page.




. Small group of adult females and a child, sitting on ground outdoors. Wearing personal-ornaments including disc-shaped lip-plugs and ear-plugs, bowl-shaped hair-styles. Two females dressing hair of other two females, using small pointed tools. Female at right holding young child.
Medium: Gelatin silver print.
Format: One of four prints mounted on album page.
